emails.subject: Re: the apartment viewing on Saturday – final tenancy details
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

Thank you for sending the signed tenancy agreement and standing-order confirmation. I’ve checked both, and everything is now in place following your viewing of the apartment on Saturday, 14 September.

To confirm the figures one final time, the monthly rent for Flat 3, 18 Mill Lane is £925, payable on the first working day of each month. Your first payment will be the agreed pro-rata amount of £462.50 for 16–30 September. I’ve also received the £1,067.30 deposit by bank transfer; it will be registered with the Deposit Protection Service within 30 days of receipt, and I’ll forward the certificate and prescribed information as soon as they issue them. No other administration or holding fee is due.

I have countersigned the document titled “Assured Shorthold Tenancy Agreement – 18 Mill Lane – 16 September” and attached the completed copy, together with the final Inventory and Schedule of Condition. I added the two points we discussed after Saturday’s viewing: the small mark on the bedroom windowsill and the loose handle on the cupboard beneath the kitchen sink. The handle is being repaired tomorrow, but I have left the note in the inventory so there is a complete record. The gas-safety certificate, electrical installation report, EPC and current How to Rent guide are included in the same attachment bundle.

Key collection is confirmed for Monday, 16 September at 17:30 at the apartment. As you mentioned that you may be coming directly from the river station, there is no problem if traffic makes you a few minutes late; just text me when you leave. I’ll bring two building-entry fobs, two sets of apartment keys and one mailbox key. We can take the opening meter readings together and sign the inventory acknowledgement then. If your gauge-maintenance call-out runs over and you cannot make 17:30, I can wait until 18:30, or leave the keys with Daniel in the ground-floor office once I have checked your photo ID in person.

The water account remains with Severn Regional Water, while electricity is currently supplied by Green Current Energy. You are free to change the electricity supplier after the tenancy begins. Council tax is Band B and should be transferred into your name from 16 September. Broadband is not included in the rent.

For completeness, your request to store your rescue-training kit in the locked basement cage is approved. The cage allocated to Flat 3 is marked “3B”; please keep wet ropes and buoyancy equipment in sealed tubs so the communal floor stays dry. Bicycles must remain in the rack rather than in the corridor.

Please reply only if any detail above differs from your understanding. Otherwise, I’ll see you at 17:30 on Monday with the keys and check-in sheet.

Best wishes,

Margaret Kendall
margaret.kendall@example.com
07700 900 418

emails.subject: Re: the glaze firing schedule — revised kiln allocation for 18–23 June
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve updated the glaze firing schedule to reflect everything we agreed in your note yesterday. The revised document is attached as “Glaze_Firing_Schedule_v12_18-23_June.pdf”, along with the final shelf plan (“Kiln2_ShelfPlan_C.pdf”). Please disregard v11, particularly the Friday unloading times.

Your six river-stone bowls and the two tall gauge-marker vases are now booked into Kiln 2 for the cone 6 oxidation firing on Tuesday 18 June. Loading will start at 4:30 pm, with candling from 6:00 pm to midnight and the main programme beginning at 6:00 am on Wednesday. Based on the last run, the kiln should reach temperature at about 3:15 pm. We won’t crack the lid before 8:00 am Thursday 20 June, and collection is scheduled for 5:30–7:00 pm that evening.

I allowed 2.5 shelves for your work rather than the two shown in the earlier version. The marker vases need 55 mm clearance from the elements, and I’d rather not squeeze the bowls beneath them. Your estimated firing contribution is therefore $42.50, comprising $35 for shelf space and $7.50 toward the slow-cool programme. That replaces the $38 estimate from 11 June. No need to transfer it separately—I’ve added it to the shared studio invoice due 28 June.

I also moved the test tiles labelled RG-14, RG-15 and RG-16 to the Saturday 22 June firing. As you pointed out, RG-15 has the revised 80/20 iron wash, so it shouldn’t be used as the reference tile for the bowls in Tuesday’s load. I’ve marked RG-12 as the reference instead. Could you please check that the handwritten labels are still legible when you drop everything off?

For delivery, the side storeroom will be open from 3:45 pm on Tuesday. If the river-gauge inspection at Bellbird Crossing runs over, leave the two padded crates on the lower green rack and text me; I can wax the remaining foot rings before loading. Please don’t leave them outside the kiln room, as the Thursday class has clay deliveries arriving in the same corridor.

One other change: Priya has withdrawn her four platters, so there is room for your three small rescue-rope mugs if they are bone dry by Monday night. I’ve tentatively listed them in Schedule C but not included them in the $42.50 total. If you add them, the contribution will rise by $9. Please confirm by 2:00 pm Monday 17 June so I can finalise the stacking diagram.

Given your swift-water training on Saturday morning, I’ve kept you off the Kiln 1 unloading roster on 22 June. I’ve swapped you with Daniel, and you’re now down to help clean and kiln-wash shelves from 6:00–7:30 pm on Sunday 23 June. Let me know if that clashes with the afternoon rescue session you mentioned.

Thanks again for catching the mismatch between the cooling log and v11. The corrected hold is 20 minutes at 1,220°C, followed by the controlled cool to 1,000°C at 80°C per hour.

Best,
Naomi Fletcher
Rivergum Consulting
naomi.fletcher@rivergumconsulting.com.au

emails.subject: Re: the costume inventory audit — final reconciliation for 18 June
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve finished the last reconciliation for the costume inventory audit ahead of our 18 June sign-off. The updated file is **Costume_Inventory_Audit_2025-06-16_v7.xlsx**, and I’ve added the supporting photographs and receipts to the folder **Audit Evidence – Final**. This version incorporates the rail-by-rail count you sent on 11 June and Priya’s corrections from Friday.

We now have 1,842 individual items recorded, with 1,796 physically verified. Of the remaining 46, 31 are confirmed as being out on loan for the summer productions, nine are awaiting identification, and six are still unaccounted for. The six missing pieces are the two red military jackets (CJ-044 and CJ-045), the green brocade waistcoat (MW-118), the child’s fox cape (AN-027), and the matching silver dance tunics (DN-203A/B). I checked the old paper issue book as you suggested, but there have been no entries against any of them since the October 2023 production.

The valuation sheet now shows a total replacement value of £68,415. That is £1,260 lower than the figure in version 6 because the three Victorian mourning dresses were duplicated under both “Women’s Period” and “Black Formal.” I removed the duplicate records rather than adjusting the individual values. I also corrected the insurance value of the beaded 1920s gown from £480 to £840, matching the appraisal dated 4 March.

There are two decisions still needed for the final report:

1. Whether to write off the six missing pieces now (£1,475 combined replacement value) or leave them open until the post-production return check on 7 July.
2. Whether the £326 spent on archival boxes and acid-free tissue should be listed as an audit expense or charged to routine wardrobe supplies.

My preference is to leave the missing items open until 7 July and classify the £326 as an audit expense, since the purchases were specifically required to address the storage issues noted during the 29 May inspection. I’ve drafted the report on that basis in **Costume_Audit_Report_Draft_16Jun.docx**, but the relevant paragraphs are highlighted so they’re easy to change.

Could you please review tabs 3 (“Exceptions”) and 6 (“Valuation”) before noon on Wednesday, 18 June? I know you said you’ll be at the upper river gauges early and have rescue training preparations in the evening, so a simple “approved” by email is enough if you don’t have time to add comments. I can then export the signed PDF and send the complete pack to the committee before the 4:00 p.m. deadline.

One final detail: the photograph labelled IMG_7714 is the navy cavalry coat, not the black frock coat. I corrected the filename in the evidence folder, but you may still see the old label if your copy synced before 9:30 this morning.

Thanks again for doing the second count of the accessories cabinet. Finding those 14 feather trims cleared nearly half the discrepancy from the 3 June worksheet.

Best,
Morgan

emails.subject: Re: the subtitling backlog — final files and remaining corrections
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve finished the last full pass on the subtitling backlog and uploaded the revised files to the shared folder under “Training Videos/Subtitles/Final Review – 18 June”. That clears the six recordings we agreed were still outstanding after your 12 June checklist.

The completed files are:

• SWR-04_River-Hazards_2024-05-11_EN-AU_v3.srt
• SWR-05_Throwbag-Drills_2024-05-11_EN-AU_v4.srt
• SWR-06_Foot-Entrapment_2024-05-18_EN-AU_v3.srt
• SWR-07_Tethered-Swimmer_2024-05-18_EN-AU_v2.srt
• Gauge-Access_Flood-Conditions_2024-05-25_EN-AU_v3.srt
• Debrief_Cedar-Bend_2024-05-25_EN-AU_v2.srt

I used the terminology sheet you sent on 14 June, so “river right”, “river left”, “PFD” and “downstream V” are now consistent throughout. I also replaced “staff gate” with “staff gauge” at 00:07:42 in the Gauge Access video and corrected the Cedar Bend location name at 00:03:19. The automatic transcript had it as “Cedar Ben” in three places.

There are four points I still need you to confirm before I mark everything closed:

1. In SWR-05 at 00:12:08, I hear “ten-metre throw line”, but the equipment list says the yellow bags contain 15-metre lines.
2. In SWR-06 at 00:18:31, the speaker’s name is unclear. I’ve left “[trainer]” rather than guessing between Callum and Colin.
3. In Gauge Access at 00:09:54, you say what sounds like “the Orana telemetry cabinet”. If Orana is the site name, should it be capitalised in the subtitle and added to the glossary?
4. In the Cedar Bend debrief at 00:16:22, the radio call sign sounds like “Rescue Two”, although your notes from 27 May say “Rescue Three”.

I’ve highlighted those captions in the accompanying document, “Subtitle_Query_Log_18-06.xlsx”. If you can add your answers in column F by Thursday, 20 June, I can make the final corrections that evening. There are only 11 caption blocks affected, so it should take less than half an hour once I have your responses.

Timing and reading speed are now within the limits we set: no more than two lines per caption, approximately 42 characters per line, and a target maximum of 20 characters per second. I split the longer safety warning in SWR-04 at 00:21:10 rather than reducing its screen time, as you asked. I also retained “[rushing water]” and the radio tone descriptions where they add useful context, but removed repeated ambient-water labels during continuous sequences.

For tracking purposes, this batch came to 287 finished minutes. Added to the 413 minutes already approved on 6 June, that brings the project total to 700 minutes. There are no unassigned videos left in the backlog folder. The two short clips labelled “Helmet Cam B” and “Boat Ramp Test” remain excluded, in line with your email of 10 June, because they’re reference footage rather than training material.

I’ve attached my invoice for the agreed remaining amount of $516.60, based on 287 minutes at $1.80 per finished minute. No rush on payment before the four queries are resolved; I mainly wanted the figures to match the completion log.

Thanks again for checking the technical wording so carefully. I know you’ve been fitting this around gauge rounds and the weekend rescue sessions, and your timestamped notes have made the final pass much easier.

Kind regards,

Leanne Mercer
Rivergum Realty
leanne.mercer@rivergumrealty.com.au

emails.subject: Re: the glaze firing schedule – final May kiln slots
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve updated the glaze firing schedule with the changes we agreed after Tuesday’s kiln check. The current version is **Glaze_Firing_Schedule_May_v9.xlsx** in the shared studio folder; please ignore v8, as that still shows your river-gauge callout weekend against the wrong firing.

Your two crates of work are now booked as follows:

• **Thursday 16 May, Kiln 2** — cone 6 oxidation, firing starts at 18:30. This is the 42-litre load with your eight blue-grey bowls, four test tiles and Jo’s six small mugs. I’ve allowed a 20-minute hold at 1200°C, as noted on your firing sheets. Estimated switch-off is 07:15 on Friday 17 May, with unloading no earlier than 16:00.

• **Tuesday 21 May, Kiln 1** — cone 6 oxidation, firing starts at 17:45. This will take the remaining seven bowls, the two lidded jars and your three river-silt glaze tests marked RS-4, RS-5 and RS-6. We’ll use the slower 100–600°C ramp you requested because of the thicker jar bases. Estimated completion is 08:30 on Wednesday 22 May; I’ve marked the kiln closed until 18:00 for cooling.

I moved the larger load off **Saturday 18 May**, since you confirmed you’re teaching the swift-water rescue session that weekend and won’t be able to do the pre-fire shelf check. Priya has taken that slot for her stoneware instead. In return, she’ll help me load Kiln 1 on the 21st, so you won’t need to leave the north gauge run early. If your Tuesday field round overruns, just text me before 16:30; I can check the foot rings and witness cones against the photographs you sent.

The only unresolved item is the RS-6 test. Its label says “cone 6, light reduction,” but both May firings are oxidation. In your message of 6 May you said oxidation was acceptable for this batch, whereas the handwritten note on the pot says to hold it for the June gas firing. I’ve left RS-6 in the green holding tray for now. Please confirm by noon on Monday 20 May whether it should go into the 21 May load or stay out for the **8 June gas firing**.

Costs have also been corrected. The 16 May shared load is **£18.40** for your portion, and the 21 May load is **£24.75**, including the £3.00 slow-ramp surcharge. Your total is therefore **£43.15**, not £46.15 as shown in v8. There’s no additional shelf-wash charge because you supplied the kiln wash last month. You can add the amount to your May studio account rather than transferring it separately.

Could you bring the first crate in by **19:00 on Wednesday 15 May**? Please put the bowls on the lower ware rack, not beside Kiln 2; Helen needs the aisle clear for the electrical inspection at 09:00 Thursday. The second crate can arrive any time before 15:30 on the 21st. I’ve printed the latest copy of **Mara_Ellis_Firing_Sheets_May.pdf** and clipped it to the kiln log, including your note that the blue-grey glaze can run if applied thicker than 1.5 mm.

Assuming RS-6 is settled, I think that finally closes the May schedule. I’ll send you the cone photographs and firing graphs after each kiln has cooled.

Best,
Megan

I’ve finished checking the seed-bank accession list against the paper packets and the freezer inventory. There are 186 accessions in total for the 2025 intake, covering 42 taxa and 17 collection sites. I also changed the grid reference for UVSB-25-103, meadowsweet from East Haugh, to NZ 18462 42791. The previous reference placed it on the opposite bank.

The six Calder Beck packets collected on 29 May were entered twice in v11. I retained UVSB-25-118 through UVSB-25-123 and removed the duplicate block numbered 124–129. The later accession numbers have therefore shifted down by six. This means the final entry, the water avens from Low Wiske collected on 9 June, is UVSB-25-186 rather than UVSB-25-192. I added an “Old provisional ID” column so labels already printed from the 11 June draft can be reconciled without guesswork.

Three items still need your confirmation before I lock the workbook:

1. UVSB-25-044, yellow flag iris, is recorded as 38 g on the envelope but 83 g on “Seed_Collections_April-May_2025.pdf.” I have provisionally used 38 g, as that matches the balance log.
2. UVSB-25-097 and UVSB-25-098 both list River Lune tributary L-4 at gauge marker 2.6 m. Was 098 actually taken at marker 2.9 m, as noted in the margin of your waterproof sheet?
3. The consent form for Fenwick Meadow, dated 7 June, permits collection of up to 250 g. Our combined cleaned weight is 263.4 g across four accessions. You mentioned that 21.8 g was retained by the landowner; if so, I’ll record the deposited quantity as 241.6 g and add that explanation to the notes.

No need to review the germination-priority column again—I incorporated your 16 June comments, including moving the 14 river-corridor accessions into the autumn trial group. I hope Saturday’s rescue-training session leaves you enough time to look at the few remaining queries, but Monday morning is still workable if the river levels keep you out longer than planned.

Thanks again for catching the willowherb identification in the earlier draft.

Best,
Natalie

emails.subject: Re: 1 July rent increase notice from Hawthorn Lettings
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve gone through the landlord’s 28 April letter, the attached Form 4 and our tenancy agreement again. The notice says the rent for 16 Millbank Terrace will rise from £1,180 to £1,345 per month from 1 July—an increase of £165, or just under 14%. That is the same figure Hawthorn Lettings quoted in their email of 2 May, so at least the paperwork and their message now match. The first version they slipped under the door on 26 April said £1,375, which is why I think we should keep all three documents.

I spoke to Priya at the tenants’ advice line this morning. She said the key issue is not simply whether the increase is steep, but whether the Form 4 was served correctly and whether £1,345 reflects the local market. Our fixed term ended on 31 January and the tenancy became monthly periodic on 1 February, so the landlord can propose an increase under section 13. However, Priya noticed that the form is dated 28 April but states it was served on 30 April. She thinks that probably still gives the required month’s notice for a 1 July start, although she wants to see the envelope and the complete form before confirming.

Could you photograph the envelope when you get home? I put it on the hall table beside the blue folder. Please include the postmark and both sides. I’ve already scanned “Rent Increase Notice – 28 April,” “Form 4 – Proposed New Rent” and the signed tenancy dated 18 January last year. I’ll forward those to Priya this afternoon along with Hawthorn’s 2 May email.

On comparable rents, I found three two-bedroom places within half a mile advertised at £1,250, £1,275 and £1,295. None has the damp patch in the back bedroom or the recurring boiler-pressure fault we reported on 12 February and again on 19 March. I’ve saved the listings as PDFs before they disappear. That should help if we negotiate or refer the proposed rent to the tribunal.

My preference is still to write to Elaine Porter before filing anything. We could offer £1,260 from 1 July, conditional on the bedroom damp being treated and the boiler repair being completed by 15 June. If they refuse, Priya says we must submit the tribunal application before the new rent is due; we should not simply pay the old amount without taking formal action. She also stressed that we should continue paying the current £1,180 in full and on time meanwhile.

I’ve drafted a response headed “Without Prejudice – Proposed Rent Increase at 16 Millbank Terrace,” but I won’t send it until you’ve checked it. I left the draft in the shared folder. Can you read it after your gauge round tomorrow? If you’re on the late callout again, just add comments and I’ll send the final version by noon on Friday, 10 May.

I know this is the last thing you need alongside the river work and Saturday’s rescue training, but we do have grounds to push back calmly. Please don’t ring Elaine from the depot; keeping everything in writing is safer.

Love,
Morgan

emails.subject: RE: Materials order RB-44718 shipped short – balance confirmed
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve now had written confirmation from our supplier regarding the short shipment against purchase order RB-44718, originally dispatched on 14 August and delivered to the Riverbend depot on 16 August.

As you recorded on the signed delivery docket DD-88164, the consignment contained only 18 of the 24 galvanised gauge-post brackets and 42 of the 50 stainless M10 x 90 mm anchor bolts ordered. The six missing brackets and eight missing bolts were also omitted from packing slip PS-44718-1, although the supplier’s tax invoice INV-70392 charged us for the complete order. The invoiced total was $3,846.70 including GST, of which $684.20 relates to the items that did not arrive.

The supplier has accepted the discrepancy on the basis of your photographs from 16 August and the count sheet you sent through last Friday. They’ve issued credit note CN-11908 for $684.20 against INV-70392 and raised replacement order SO-44718-B at no additional cost. I’ve attached copies of both documents for your records.

The balance is booked to leave their Brisbane warehouse on Tuesday, 3 September, via Northline consignment NGE284771. Their current estimate is delivery to Riverbend between 5 and 6 September. I’ve asked them to label the two cartons “BALANCE OF PO RB-44718 – HOLD FOR MARA ELLIS” so they aren’t combined with the routine stores delivery again. There should be one carton containing the six brackets and a smaller carton containing the eight bolts, together with revised packing slip PS-44718-2.

Could you please check the quantities before signing the carrier’s docket? In particular, the brackets should be the 320 mm hot-dip galvanised type shown on specification sheet GWB-320 Rev C, not the shorter 250 mm version they tried to substitute in July. If either carton is damaged or the count is still wrong, note it on the docket and send me a photo before the driver leaves if practical.

Accounts has put the original invoice on hold rather than paying it less the shortage. Once you confirm that the balance has arrived, I’ll have them apply CN-11908 and release the corrected net amount of $3,162.50. That will keep the PO, goods receipt and invoice aligned in our system.

I appreciate this has held up the bracket replacements planned for the North Fork and Mill Crossing gauge sites. The supplier has agreed to reimburse up to $95 for any additional depot-to-site freight caused by the split delivery, so please retain the transport receipt if you need to make a separate run. There is no need for your team to absorb that cost against the gauge maintenance allocation.

Please let me know when the cartons land, or if the tracking has not updated by the afternoon of 4 September. I’ll chase their dispatch manager directly if there’s another delay.

Kind regards,

Narelle Bishop
Property and Procurement Coordinator
Riverbend Property Services
narelle.bishop@riverbendproperty.com.au

emails.subject: Harbour pilot certification renewal – medical accepted and final assessment booking
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

A quick update on your harbour pilot certification renewal: the Port Authority has now accepted the replacement medical certificate from Dr Chen dated 18 September 2025. They have also matched it to your renewal application HPCR-25-0417, so you can disregard the automated deficiency notice issued on 22 September. That notice crossed with the corrected upload and no further medical information is required.

The remaining item is the practical assessment. Captain Doyle has reserved the 07:00–10:30 session on Thursday, 9 October aboard the Southern Kestrel, departing from Berth 4 at East Harbour. emails.subject: Re: 14 September rent increase notice – revised figures
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

Thanks for sending the clearer scan of the landlord’s 14 September notice and the tenancy agreement you signed on 1 April 2022. I have compared them with the rent schedule attached to your message from Monday.

As we discussed, the notice says the monthly rent for 18 Mill Lane will rise from £925 to £1,075 with effect from 1 November. That is an increase of £150 a month, or just over 16%. However, clause 7.2 of the tenancy agreement says the rent may be reviewed once in any twelve-month period and that you must receive at least two full calendar months’ written notice. The previous increase, from £875 to £925, took effect on 1 February this year, so the proposed 1 November date appears inconsistent with both parts of that clause.

There is also a discrepancy between the figures in the documents. The covering letter headed “Annual Rent Review 2024” gives the new rent as £1,075, while the attached standing-order slip says £1,050 from 1 November. I would not amend your standing order until the landlord confirms in writing which amount is actually being proposed and provides a valid effective date. Continue paying the current £925 on the first of each month in the meantime, and keep the funds for any disputed difference aside.

I have drafted a response below for you to send to Mr Pritchard or Greenbank Lettings:

“Dear Mr Pritchard,

I acknowledge receipt of your rent increase notice dated 14 September 2024. The notice proposes increasing the rent for 18 Mill Lane from £925 to £1,075 per calendar month from 1 November 2024. The accompanying standing-order instruction instead states £1,050.

Please clarify the intended amount. I also draw your attention to clause 7.2 of the tenancy agreement dated 1 April 2022, which provides for no more than one review in a twelve-month period and requires at least two full calendar months’ written notice. As the last increase took effect on 1 February 2024, I do not agree that the proposed increase can take effect on 1 November 2024.

Until this is resolved and a compliant notice is served, I will continue paying the contractual rent of £925 per calendar month. This should not be taken as agreement to the proposed increase.

Yours sincerely,
Mara Ellis”

If the landlord intended to use the statutory procedure rather than the contractual review clause, ask Greenbank to send the prescribed Form 4; the two-page letter you received is not that form. A valid statutory notice would ordinarily need to allow at least one month and could not take effect before the end of the fixed or contractual restriction that applies. I would avoid stating an alternative acceptable figure for now, as that could muddy your position.

Please also save the original envelope showing the 18 September postmark, along with the PDF named “Rent Review Notice - Mill Lane.pdf.” If they telephone, make a brief note of the date, time and what was said, then ask them to confirm it by email. Do not feel pressured to agree during a call.

Send me their reply when it arrives. If they insist that £1,075 is due on 1 November or threaten arrears action, I can help you put the papers in order for the council’s tenancy-relations officer.

Best,
Helen

emails.subject: Re: 14 June fermentation batch — temperature excursion review
emails.content:
Hi,

I have now reconciled the logger export with the handwritten readings for Batch F-0614, the 120 L elderflower-and-ginger ferment that overshot temperature on 16 June. The corrected timeline is in “F-0614_Temperature_Excursion_v7.pdf,” which replaces v6 from Tuesday.

The vessel was pitched at 18.4°C at 19:20 on 14 June. It remained between 18.1°C and 19.6°C until 22:40 on 15 June, then rose steadily after the cooling-loop valve stuck. The probe recorded 24.0°C at 01:50 on 16 June, 27.8°C at 04:10, and a maximum of 29.3°C at 05:35. Your 05:42 manual reading of 29.1°C confirms that the logger was not simply drifting. Once you freed the valve and circulated the two 10 L ice-water containers, the batch fell below 24°C at 08:25 and reached 20.2°C by 13:10. Total time above our 24°C limit was 6 hours 35 minutes, including 2 hours 20 minutes above 27°C.

I also corrected the earlier note about the sugar addition. We added 8.6 kg, not 9.0 kg, giving an original gravity of 1.046. Yesterday’s final gravity was 1.008 in both samples after temperature correction, so attenuation is about 83%. The retained bottle opened normally: no gush, rope, film, or solvent aroma. There is a little more pear/banana ester than in Batch F-0524, but the panel of four did not identify harsh fusel alcohol. pH moved from 4.18 at pitching to 3.36 on 21 June, which is consistent with the previous batches.

Micro results from Northbank came back this morning. The report “NB-24-1887_F0614.pdf” shows no detectable coliforms or enteric organisms, and the yeast morphology is consistent with the production culture. The low-level Lactobacillus signal was also present in the control blank, so the lab has marked it as probable handling contamination rather than evidence of spoilage. I have attached their amended certificate, dated 27 June, along with “F-0614_Sensory_Scores.xlsx.”

On that basis, I agree with your proposal not to dump the full 112 L remaining after sampling. Please keep it quarantined and clearly tagged until we complete the 72-hour package check. I filled twelve 330 mL test bottles at 15:00 today: six will stay at 20°C and six at 30°C. I’ll check pressure, pH, aroma, and visible growth at 24, 48, and 72 hours. If there is no abnormal pressure rise and pH remains within 0.10 of today’s value, we can release it for the volunteer event, but not before Monday, 1 July.

For the root cause, I have changed the wording from “operator failed to monitor” to “cooling valve mechanical seizure compounded by alarm-routing failure.” The alarm did trigger at 24°C, but it went only to the retired tablet in the store room. That matches the notification log you sent. Please confirm that the replacement valve installed on 22 June is the stainless V2 unit, serial CV-4471, and that the high-temperature alert now reaches both your phone and mine. Once confirmed, I’ll close actions 3 and 4 in “CAPA_F-0614_revC.docx.”

Thanks again for getting there at 05:40 after your gauge round. Without the manual check and rapid cooling, we would almost certainly have lost the batch.

Best,
Mara

emails.subject: Re: Rent increase notice dated 14 August
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve gone through the landlord’s rent increase notice again and compared it with the lease and our earlier emails. The notice dated 14 August says the weekly rent will rise from $520 to $585 from 21 October—an increase of $65 a week, or 12.5%. That matches the amount in Priya’s covering email, although the first version she attached on Monday incorrectly listed the commencement date as 21 September. I’ve saved both versions, including the corrected PDF titled “Notice of Rent Increase – 17 Calder Street – amended.pdf”.

As you pointed out, our fixed-term agreement runs until 3 November. I rang Tenants Advice this morning, and they confirmed that the increase cannot take effect during the current fixed term unless the agreement expressly provides for both the timing and method of calculation. Clause 7 says only that the rent is $520 per week; there is no rent-review formula. On that basis, 21 October appears to be too early even if the required notice period has otherwise been met.

They suggested that we reply in writing rather than discuss it by phone. We should ask Priya to confirm that the proposed increase will not commence before 4 November and request the evidence the landlord relied on to arrive at $585. The three “comparable properties” mentioned in her email are all renovated three-bedroom houses. Ours has two bedrooms, the back room still has the ceiling damage from the February leak, and the garage has been unusable since the door motor failed on 6 June. Those differences seem relevant if we need to argue that the amount is excessive.

I’ve drafted the following response:

“Thank you for the amended notice dated 14 August. We do not agree that the proposed rent of $585 per week can commence on 21 October, as our fixed-term tenancy continues until 3 November and the agreement contains no provision permitting an increase during that term. Please confirm that no increase will apply before 4 November. We also request copies or details of the comparable rental evidence used to determine the proposed amount, taking account of the property’s size, condition and outstanding repairs.”

Are you happy for me to send that from both of us tomorrow? I’d prefer not to add a counteroffer yet. Tenants Advice said we can challenge the amount separately, but the application deadline runs from receipt of the notice, so I’ve marked 13 September as the date by which we should decide whether to lodge. I’ve put the notice, lease, repair emails and current local listings in the shared “Calder St rent” folder.

Also, Priya asked whether she could call at 4:30 tomorrow. I told her you’d be out checking the Upper Murren gauges and might not have reception, so I haven’t agreed to a time. Keeping this in email seems safest anyway.

Let me know if you want anything changed in the draft, especially the wording about the damaged ceiling and garage.

Narelle

emails.subject: Re: 18 May saison batch – temperature overshoot review
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve finished checking the 18 May saison batch against the Tilt export and your notes from the shed controller. You were right about the timing: the 62 L batch rose from 23.8°C at 21:10 on 19 May to a peak of 31.6°C at 03:42 on 20 May. It stayed above 30°C for approximately 2 hours 25 minutes, rather than the four hours I estimated in my last message. The probe started reporting normally again after you reseated it at 06:15, so I have not discarded the later readings.

I’ve attached the corrected files as “Saison_18May_Temperature_Log_v3.csv” and “Batch_24-05_Deviation_Report_v2.pdf”. The report now records the actual pitching amount (two 11.5 g packets of BE-134), the starting gravity of 1.052, and the 58 L transferred after trub loss. I also amended the cooling-water entry from 20 L to 27 L, based on the marks in your brew-day notebook.

The good news is that yesterday’s samples from bottles 3 and 11 were consistent. Both finished at 1.006, with pH readings of 4.18 and 4.21. I picked up a little extra pear/banana aroma, but no solvent character, sourness or obvious contamination. Carbonation in bottle 11 was lively, although it had been at room temperature for longer. I agree with your suggestion that we keep the batch quarantined until the next check rather than tipping it solely because of the temperature excursion.

Could you bring one unopened 500 ml bottle from the warmest crate and one from the lower shelf when you come over on Saturday, 8 June? I’ll chill both for 24 hours, then we can compare them at the 16:30 tasting. I’ve added a line for each sample to “Saison_18May_Sensory_Sheet.docx”. If either shows pressure, phenolic notes beyond the expected saison character, or a pH below 4.0, we’ll stop and dispose of the remaining 41 bottles.

On the controller fault, I tested the Inkbird with the spare probe in a water bath this morning. The relay opened correctly at 24.5°C three times, which makes your loose-probe theory more likely than a failed controller. For the next batch I suggest taping the probe firmly to the fermenter under insulation, setting the high alarm to 26°C, and using the separate blue logger as an independent check. I’ve put those steps into “Fermentation_Setup_Checklist_v4.pdf”.

Please don’t leave the bottles in the gauge van while you’re on the Friday route; even a mild afternoon could warm them enough to muddy the comparison. If Saturday changes because of rescue training, just text me and I’ll collect them from your porch in the insulated box.

Thanks again for catching the discrepancy in the log.

Best,
Natalie

emails.subject: Re: 17 May fermentation batch – temperature overshoot
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve finished reviewing the logger export and your notes for the 17 May ginger saison batch. You were right that the temperature overshoot was shorter than the first graph suggested. The probe climbed above the 22.0°C set point at 01:42 on 19 May, peaked at 28.6°C at 03:18, and was back below 24.0°C by 06:51. The flat section in the screenshot you sent on Monday was a charting artefact, not another four hours at peak temperature.

I’ve attached the corrected “Batch_17May_TempLog_v3.csv” and updated the incident sheet as “Fermentation_Deviation_17May_revB.pdf”. I also added your observation that the cooling jacket outlet hose had kinked behind the crate. On the evidence we have, the controller relay operated normally; the restricted return flow is still the most likely cause. The 26 L batch started at an original gravity of 1.054, and yesterday’s reading of 1.011 is consistent with the expected attenuation rather than an uncontrolled secondary fermentation.

The samples tell much the same story. Bottle A, drawn before the temperature rise, was clean but still quite sweet. Bottle B, drawn at 18:30 on 19 May after cooling, had a stronger pear/banana note but no solvent character, sourness or visible pellicle. The pH moved from 4.62 at pitching to 4.08 on 20 May and 3.96 on 23 May. I don’t see a safety reason to dump it, although the warmer interval will probably make it fruitier than the April trial.

My suggestion is to leave it at 20°C until the gravity is unchanged for two consecutive days, then cold-crash as planned. Please don’t package on the strength of the single 1.011 reading. If Friday morning’s result is still 1.011 (or within one point), the original 5.5 g/L priming rate should remain suitable. That works out to 143 g for the full 26 L, but recalculate against the actual volume after transfer rather than adding the whole amount automatically.

I’ve also revised the checklist we discussed. The new version includes a hose-clearance check, a high-temperature alarm at 24.5°C, and a separate independent probe taped to the vessel under insulation. For the next run, I’d test the alarm with water before pitching rather than discovering another notification problem overnight. The missed alert was traced to the old email rule, so I’ve replaced your obsolete work address with mara.ellis@example.org in the controller account.

Could you confirm whether the backup probe was sitting against the stainless wall or hanging free in the chamber? Its maximum was only 25.1°C, and that placement detail will help us explain the 3.5°C difference in the close-out note.

I can collect Bottle C after my Hawthorn culvert inspection on Thursday, probably around 16:45. If you’re still out servicing the upstream gauges, leave it in the labelled box in the shed fridge and I’ll message before I come through. No need to interrupt your rescue-training preparation on Saturday.

Regards,
Priya Nair
Riverland Civil

emails.subject: Re: 14 February miso batch — temperature overshoot and salvage notes
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve compared your latest readings with the photos and the log sheet you sent. For the 14 February chickpea-miso batch, the key excursion still appears to be the period between 22:40 on 15 February and 04:20 on 16 February. The centre probe rose from 31.8°C to a recorded maximum of 41.6°C, while the shelf probe reached 38.9°C. That fits with your note that the 2.4 kg tray was still covered with the folded towel and pushed close to the heat mat overnight.

The good news is that nothing in the 16 February photos suggests obvious contamination. The growth was evenly white, the beans were knitting together, and I couldn’t see the green, black or pink patches we discussed. Your pH readings—5.9 before incubation, 5.1 after the overshoot and 4.7 when you mixed in the brine on 17 February—also moved in the expected direction. The smell you described as “sweet chestnut with a sharp pear note” is less concerning than ammonia, rotten meat or a strongly solvent-like odour would be.

That said, photographs and pH strips cannot establish that a batch is safe. As agreed, please don’t taste it or give any to the dogs. Keep the three 750 ml jars labelled “14FEB-CM-A/B/C” sealed in the utility-room fridge until the culture result is back. I dropped your 25 g sample from jar B at the lab yesterday morning; their receipt is attached as “WSV_LabReceipt_1847_21Feb.pdf”. They expect the mould identification and basic bacterial screen by Tuesday, 27 February.

I also reviewed “Koji_Temp_Log_v4.xlsx”. Your correction of the 03:10 entry from 46.1°C to 41.6°C makes sense given the probe photo and the adjacent readings. Please retain the original file as well as v4, just so we have an unaltered record. In the incident note, I’d phrase it as a five-hour-forty-minute excursion above 35°C, not as six hours above 40°C; only the 02:30 and 03:10 centre readings exceeded 40°C.

For the replacement batch, your proposed changes look sensible: divide the 2.4 kg into two shallow trays, leave at least 8 cm between them, remove the towel once the centre reaches 30°C, and set the controller alarm at 33°C. I’d also move the independent probe into the middle of the bean layer rather than taping it under the tray. Since you’ll be at the Mill Weir rescue-training day on Saturday, I would wait until Sunday evening to inoculate rather than leave the first active phase unattended. The river-gauge alarm is enough to have on your phone without adding a ferment alarm too.

One small correction to my previous message: the salt calculation for 3.6 kg finished mix should be 396 g at 11%, not 360 g. Your actual addition was 398 g, so no action is needed; please just amend the figure in “Chickpea_Miso_Batch_Record_14Feb.docx”.

I’ll message as soon as the lab report arrives. If any jar lid domes, leaks, or develops a markedly foul smell before then, don’t open it—bag the whole jar and let me know.

Best,

Priya

Priya Nair, BVetMed MRCVS
Westside Veterinary Practice

The notice dated 12 June says the monthly rent will rise from £1,180 to £1,365 with effect from 1 September. That is an increase of £185 a month, or 15.7%. It also says the first payment at the new rate is due on 1 September, but our tenancy began on 15 October 2022 and the current fixed term runs until 14 October this year. Clause 7.2 of the signed agreement says rent may be reviewed “on each anniversary of the commencement date,” so I still don’t see how they can impose the increase six weeks before the anniversary unless we agree to it.

There’s another inconsistency: the attached document, “Notice of Rent Adjustment – Flat 3B,” refers to clause 8.1. Our copy has clause 8.1 covering access for repairs, not rent reviews. I’ve highlighted that, along with the incorrect move-in date of 1 September 2022. Please keep the original PDF and the envelope; the postmark is 14 June, despite the notice saying it was served on 12 June.

I spoke briefly with the council’s tenancy advice line this morning. They wouldn’t give a formal opinion without seeing the documents, but they said we should not sign the “Rent Variation Acceptance Form” or start paying £1,365 while disputing the effective date. Their suggestion was to continue paying the existing £1,180 on time and ask the agent to confirm in writing whether this is intended as a contractual review, a proposed variation, or a statutory notice. They also said that if it is meant to be a statutory notice, it needs to be on the prescribed form rather than the agency’s own one-page letter.

I’ve drafted this response:

“We acknowledge receipt of the notice dated 12 June proposing an increase from £1,180 to £1,365 per calendar month from 1 September. We do not agree to the proposed variation or its effective date. Our tenancy commenced on 15 October 2022, and clause 7.2 provides for review on the anniversary of that date. Please clarify the contractual or statutory basis for the increase, correct the commencement date and clause reference, and provide any prescribed notice on the required form. Pending clarification, we will continue paying the contractual rent of £1,180.”

Are you happy for me to send that to Priya Shah and copy Daniel Mercer, or would you rather send it from your address because Priya’s 18 June email was addressed directly to you? I’d like it to go today if possible, certainly before their requested acceptance deadline of Friday, 28 June.

Separately, I checked comparable listings. The two-bedroom flat on Alder Street is advertised at £1,275, and the one above the pharmacy is £1,300, both with parking. That makes £1,365 difficult to justify, especially with the bedroom leak reported under repair ticket AP-4471 still unresolved since 6 May. If they are willing to negotiate from 15 October, I think offering £1,260 would be reasonable, with any agreement conditional on the leak and damaged plaster being repaired first.

Call me when you’re back from the gauge run. I’m free after 6:30, apart from the rescue training planning call at 8.

Morgan

emails.subject: Re: 14 May fermentation batch temperature overshoot — revised log and next steps
emails.content:
Hi,

I’ve finished checking the records for the fermentation batch started on 14 May and have updated the attached document, “Batch F-24-0514 Temperature Excursion Review v3.” The short version is that the vessel held at the 22.0°C set point until 01:35 on 16 May, then rose steadily and peaked at 31.7°C at 04:18. It remained above our 26.0°C upper limit for 2 hours 43 minutes, rather than the 90 minutes I estimated in my last message.

The most likely cause is still the combination of the active fermentation phase and the failed cooling-water solenoid. The controller was calling for cooling from 01:42 onward, but the valve-position trace stayed at 4–6%. When I tested solenoid SV-3 on 17 May, the coil was receiving 24 V but the plunger was sticking. I’ve added those readings, along with the controller export, to “F-24-0514 Sensor and Alarm Log.csv.” The independent probe was within 0.3°C of the vessel sensor, so this does not appear to have been a bad temperature reading.

For completeness, the batch contained 118 L at the start, made with 24.5 kg of substrate and inoculated with 2.4 L of starter. We lost approximately 3 L during sampling and transfer, leaving 115 L currently held in the cold room at 4.2°C. The 18 May sample showed pH 3.61, compared with 3.74 before the excursion. Aroma is sharper than normal but there is no visible contamination, film, or unexpected gas production. I’ve labelled all six retained 250 mL samples “HOLD — TEMP EXCURSION” and recorded their shelf positions in the review.

I agree with your suggestion not to discard anything until the laboratory results are back. The yeast and bacterial screens were delivered this morning under chain-of-custody form COC-1846; the lab expects preliminary results by Thursday, 23 May, and the full panel by 27 May. Please don’t use Batch F-24-0514 for the planned 25 May blending trial unless we both sign off after those results.

I’ve also revised the corrective-action section. Before the next run, I propose that we replace SV-3, test the high-temperature alarm at 25.5°C, and add a second alert if the cooling demand remains above 80% for more than ten minutes without a corresponding valve response. I can fit the replacement solenoid on Wednesday afternoon. The quoted part is £68.40, plus the new gasket at £6.75.

Could you review sections 4 and 6 of the excursion report, particularly the disposition criteria? If you’re comfortable with the wording, I’ll issue the final version after the lab report arrives. I’ve kept the original 16 May log and v2 of the review in the batch folder so the audit trail is intact.

Thanks for catching the discrepancy in the alarm duration. Your reconstruction from the five-minute logger data was right; I had initially used the dashboard summary, which omitted the first 37 minutes above 26.0°C.

Best,
Mara Ellis

emails.subject: Re: the shared storage locker at the marina — renewal and inventory
emails.content:

The annual charge has gone up from £384 to £420, including VAT. As we agreed in December, I’m happy to continue splitting it equally, so that would be £210 each. I’ve attached the document she sent over, “B17_Storage_Renewal_2025-26.pdf.” I checked the contact details and corrected the mobile number they still had for you from the old paper form. Could you look over sections 4 and 7, especially the wording about fuel containers and rescue equipment? The prohibition on petrol is unchanged, but section 7 now says wet ropes, PFDs and dry suits must be drained before storage. I assume that won’t be a problem with the training kit, but you’ll know better than I do.

Leanne also found our £60 key deposit on the account, so we do not need to pay that again. Payment is due by 28 February. If it suits you, I can pay the full £420 by bank transfer and you can send me your £210 share afterward, as we did last year. Please don’t transfer anything until I confirm that the marina has accepted the signed agreement.

On the inventory: I went down to B-17 on Sunday, 2 February and compared the contents with the list we made on 19 October. Your two yellow rope bags, the red throwline crate, four blue PFDs and the folding drying rack are all there. My kayak trolley, grey tool chest and the two plastic paddle bins are also accounted for. I couldn’t find the small orange first-aid dry bag that was listed on the October sheet. Is that the one you took for the January swift-water session? There is an unlabelled orange bag on the upper shelf, but it contains pulley hardware rather than medical supplies.

I moved your gauge-maintenance waders off the concrete and onto the lower rack after noticing a little damp along the back wall. Nothing appears damaged. Leanne said the gutter above the B row was cleared on 30 January, and she logged my report as maintenance ticket MAR-2517. She asked us to leave a 10 cm gap behind the shelving until they inspect the wall next Tuesday, 11 February. I’ve done that on the left side, but the paddle bins still need shifting forward slightly.

I can meet you there at 17:45 on Wednesday, 12 February to finish the inventory, label the orange bag and sign the renewal. If you’re on late gauge rounds after the forecast rain, Saturday the 15th at 10:00 would also work, although that would be after the office’s requested return date. In that case, I can sign my copy on Wednesday and leave it with Leanne for you.

Let me know which option works, and whether the missing first-aid bag is with you.

Best,
Morgan

emails.subject: Re: the apartment viewing on Saturday
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

Thanks for checking with the agent. Saturday 17 August at 10:30 am works for me, and I’ll meet you outside the main entrance at 18 Kurilpa Street about ten minutes beforehand. I’ve saved Daniel Cho’s number in case the inspection runs late or he has trouble finding us on the list.

The rent is definitely $610 per week, not $630 as it briefly showed on the app, and Daniel confirmed that the four-week bond will be $2,440. He also said they want the successful applicants to start the lease on Monday 26 August, although there may be a few days’ flexibility if we ask at the viewing. A 12-month term would suit me better than the six-month option.

I’ve completed most of the Form 22 application draft and uploaded my passport, last three West Brisbane Vet payslips and the employment letter from Dr Patel. I’ll bring printed copies on Saturday as well. Could you bring your photo ID and the water authority employment confirmation you mentioned? Daniel said we can submit one joint application after the viewing, but each of us still needs separate proof-of-income and rental-reference sections. I’ve listed Helen Walsh from my current tenancy as my reference and warned her that the agency may call next week.

There are a few things I’d like us to check in person: whether the second bedroom actually fits a queen bed and desk, how much traffic noise reaches the balcony, and whether the single car space is allocated or first come, first served. I also want to test the air-conditioning in both bedrooms and look for damp around the laundry wall. Your point about the building’s lower garage being close to the 2022 flood extent was a good one. Daniel’s email says water entered the driveway but not the residential levels, so perhaps you can ask the more technical follow-up questions about drainage and the backflow gate.

The agent confirmed that indoor cats are considered with body-corporate approval. That’s reassuring for Nori, though I won’t include her on the application until we’ve seen the balcony screens and confirmed the pet process. The listing’s “secure storage” is apparently a lockable cage behind the parking bay rather than a separate room, so it may not be suitable for your rescue gear if it stays damp. We should measure it before assuming your ropes and PFD tubs will fit.

I’ve booked Saturday morning off at the clinic, but I need to leave by 11:40 am for the noon surgical handover. If Daniel is happy, could we walk to the nearby café straight after the inspection and make a decision there? That should give us enough time to compare notes and, if we both agree, submit the application before the 2:00 pm deadline he mentioned. I’m comfortable splitting the rent $305 each, with electricity and internet equally divided; we can discuss the car space separately since I’ll only need it for late clinic shifts.

Please send me a message if your Friday gauge run changes your availability. Otherwise, I’ll see you at 10:20 on Saturday outside number 18.

Best,
Priya

The revised package is named “Q2_2025_Hydrology_Dataset_v4.zip”; please use that version rather than v3, which still contains the provisional Millbrook values.

There are 18,426 fifteen-minute observations across the 14 active stations. I restored 32 missing records at gauge RB-07 (Millbrook) for 16–17 May using the field logger download, not interpolation. I also shifted the 24 April records from gauge LN-03 (Lower Nent) forward by one hour after confirming that the replacement logger had remained on GMT. That resolves the timestamp mismatch you spotted between “Q2_2025_StageFlow_v3.csv” and the telemetry archive.

The stage correction for WR-12 (West Rindle) is now included. The pressure-transducer offset changed from +0.018 m to +0.024 m following the 11 June staff-gauge check, so 6,912 stage values from 20 April through 30 June were recalculated. Corresponding discharge values were regenerated with rating curve RC-WR12-2024B. The quarter’s revised maximum is 86.4 m³/s at 03:15 on 22 May; the previous export showed 88.1 m³/s.

I left the 7–9 June gap at AF-02 (Ash Ford) flagged as missing because both the telemetry feed and local logger failed during the battery fault. As agreed in your note on Monday, those 201 records have not been infilled. The QA field uses code “M-EQUIP,” and the station note references work order WA-25176. There are also nine “ICE/DEBRIS” flags at North Weir from the 6 April inspection; those are valid and should remain.

The package contains:

• Q2_2025_StageFlow_v4.csv
• Q2_2025_DailyMeans_v4.csv
• Q2_2025_QA_Log_v4.xlsx
• Q2_2025_Station_Metadata.pdf
• Q2_2025_Change_Summary_v3-v4.txt
• SHA256SUMS.txt

The checksum for the main StageFlow file begins “7c91b6e4” and the CSV contains 18,426 data rows plus the header. I’ve retained the units we agreed on—stage in metres, discharge in m³/s, and rainfall in millimetres—with timestamps in UTC using the ISO 8601 format. No station coordinates or rating-curve identifiers have changed since the 3 July metadata sheet.

Two items still need your confirmation before the submission copy is marked final: whether the authority wants the uncorrected sensor stage for WR-12 included as a separate audit column, and whether the quarterly summary should quote 97.8% or 98.0% overall completeness. The exact figure is 97.84%; v3 rounded to one decimal place, while the reporting template displays whole percentages.

If there are no further changes, I’ll rename the package “Q2_2025_Hydrology_Dataset_FINAL.zip” and place it in the quarterly archive by 16:00 on Friday, 11 July. Please don’t send v3 to Data Services in the meantime.

Mara Ellis
Hydrology Technician
Regional Water Authority

I’ve now heard back from Leanne at Harbourside Property about the rent increase notice we received from Mr Kellett on 14 June.

As you spotted, the original notice said the weekly rent would rise from $520 to $590 from 1 August, which was only 48 days after the notice was issued. Leanne has acknowledged that this did not provide the required 60 days’ notice. She has attached a replacement document titled “Notice of Rent Increase – 18 June 2025 (Revised)” and withdrawn the 14 June version.

The revised notice sets the increase at $565 per week, starting on 18 August 2025. That is $25 less than the amount in the original notice, although still a $45 weekly increase on our current rent. Leanne says the figure was reconsidered after we sent the three comparable listings from Wattle Street and Bridge Road on Monday. She has also confirmed that our current payment of $520 remains due each Friday up to and including 15 August; the first $565 payment will be due on Friday, 22 August, with the three days from 18–20 August adjusted separately on the ledger. I’ve asked her to spell out that pro-rata amount rather than leave us to calculate it.

There are two points I have not agreed to yet. First, the revised notice still describes the property as including “secure undercover parking,” despite the garage roller door having been out of service since 27 May. Second, Leanne’s email says the $565 figure is “non-negotiable,” but she hasn’t provided the rental appraisal Mr Kellett referred to when he called last week. I replied asking for the appraisal and for written confirmation that the garage repair scheduled for 2 July is actually booked.

I’ve saved both notices, Leanne’s email, and the listings in the shared tenancy folder under “Rent increase 2025.” Please keep the original 14 June notice even though they have withdrawn it; the tenants’ advice line said we should retain the full paper trail in case the dates or ledger entries are disputed later.

Unless you object, I’ll send a joint response by 5 pm Thursday saying that we acknowledge receipt of the revised notice but reserve our position on whether $565 reflects the property’s current condition. I’ll also propose $550 per week from 18 August, conditional on the garage door and the leaking kitchen tap being repaired before then. That seems more defensible than the $540 we discussed on Sunday, given the nearby two-bedroom at 31 Wattle Street has now been listed at $555.

Could you check the revised notice tonight, especially the tenant names and lease dates? It lists our fixed term as ending 30 September 2025, which matches my copy of the agreement, but I’d rather have both of us verify everything before replying. Also let me know whether you’re comfortable with the $550 counteroffer or want to hold at $540.

I’ll be at the depot until about 4 tomorrow checking the telemetry units, but I can call after that if it’s easier.

Thanks,
Narelle

emails.subject: Re: 14 May saison batch — temperature overshoot review
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve now compared your gauge-logger export with my notes for the saison batch that overshot on 14 May. Your reconstruction was right: the fermenter did not sit at 31°C all night, as I first feared. According to “Batch-24-05-14_TempLog.csv,” the probe crossed our 22.5°C upper limit at 21:42, reached a maximum of 30.8°C at 23:17, and fell below 25°C again at 01:06 after we moved the vessel into the utility-room bath. Total time above 25°C was 2 hours 49 minutes.

The important correction is that I pitched at 18:35, not 19:10. I found the original entry on the paper brew sheet; the later time in “Saison_Batch_Record_v3.docx” was when I fitted the airlock. That means the temperature rise started about three hours after pitching, which makes active fermentation a more plausible contributor than the heater alone. Could you amend the timeline table before we circulate it to Ben?

I also tested the controller yesterday using your suggested jug-and-ice-bath check. At 0.4°C on the reference thermometer, the controller displayed 2.1°C; at 20.0°C it displayed 21.6°C. The separate blue probe was within 0.3°C at both points. More worryingly, the relay remained energised until the displayed temperature reached 24.7°C even though the set point was 21.5°C with a 0.5°C differential. I’ve labelled that controller “DO NOT USE” and removed it from the cupboard.

For completeness, the batch volume was 23 litres, not 25, and we added 11 g of Belle Saison yeast. Gravity has gone from 1.052 to 1.006. The sample this morning had a strong pear aroma but no solvent or burnt-plastic note, so I don’t think we need to discard it yet. I propose leaving it at 20°C until 21 May, then taking another gravity reading and a small tasting sample. I won’t bottle anything unless the reading is unchanged for three days.

I’ve attached my revised incident note, “Fermentation_Temp_Excursion_14May_v4.pdf,” plus photographs of the controller display and probe positions. In section 3 I retained your observation that the stainless thermowell lagged the taped external probe by roughly 18 minutes during cooling. Please check that I have described your method accurately; I know you were adapting the same sort of sanity-check you use when a river-gauge logger starts drifting, but I don’t want to overstate the precision.

One remaining question: your graph shows a brief drop from 27.4°C to 24.9°C at 22:31, then an immediate return to 27.2°C. Do you think that is when I lifted the probe while adding the wet towels, or should we flag it as a missing/invalid reading? My handwritten note says “wrap on 22:28,” so the timing fits. I’d rather annotate it than silently smooth it out.

If you can send the corrected timeline by Friday afternoon, I’ll add the sensory notes and forward the complete record to Ben. There’s no hurry tonight, especially if you’re out checking the upstream gauges after the rain.

Thanks again for turning my rather panicked messages into something usable.

Best,
Natalie

emails.subject: Re: 14 May saison batch — temperature overshoot review
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

I’ve gone through the Tilt export and your notes for the 14 May saison batch. The temperature rise is clearer now: the 23 L batch held at 20.5–21.2 °C from pitching at 19:40 on Tuesday until about 03:10 Thursday, then climbed steadily while you were away on the Bellbird gauge call-out. It crossed 26 °C at 05:48 and peaked at 31.6 °C at 08:22 before you moved the fermenter into the laundry tub. That matches the timestamps in “Saison_14May_Tilt.csv” and the photo of the Inkbird display you sent on Sunday.

I don’t think we need to tip it. The gravity was already down from 1.054 to 1.018 before the sharpest part of the rise, and your latest reading of 1.006 suggests the yeast finished rather than stalled. The sample’s pear/pepper character sounds normal for Belle Saison; the slight solvent note may soften with conditioning. I’d leave it at 22 °C through 24 May, then take two hydrometer readings 24 hours apart. If both are within one point, cold-crash gradually to 4 °C rather than dropping it all at once.

On the cause: your “Fermentation Controller Checksheet v2” says the cooling outlet tested correctly on 12 May, so I agree the controller itself probably wasn’t the initial fault. The more likely sequence is that the fridge compressor tried to start during the warm-up, the loose double adaptor interrupted supply, and the 40 W heat belt remained energised because it was plugged into the separate power board. Your note that the fridge light was off when you returned at 09:05 supports that. Please retire that adaptor rather than trying to tighten the contacts.

For the replacement setup, I’d make three changes:

1. Plug the fridge directly into the Inkbird cooling socket, with no adaptor or extension between them.
2. Set the heating differential to 0.5 °C and cooling differential to 1.0 °C, with a 10-minute compressor delay.
3. Put the probe under a folded foam pad against the fermenter wall, not hanging in the chamber air.

I’ve added those points to “Batch 07 Temperature Incident Notes – draft 2.docx”. I also corrected the quantity of dry yeast from 11 g to 11.5 g and recorded your 18 May taste sample as 120 mL. Could you confirm whether the heat belt was around the lower third of the vessel or directly beneath it? Your sketch and the photo appear to differ, and I want the final note to be accurate.

If it tastes clean enough on 24 May, I’d prime conservatively at 5.5 g/L—about 126 g dextrose for the estimated 22.9 L remaining. Given how attenuative this strain is, use the pressure-rated bottles and keep the first week’s conditioning crate somewhere contained. Bring one bottle when we meet after your Sunday rescue session; I’m curious whether the hot phase has produced more ester than the room-temperature sample suggests.

Regards,
Priya

emails.subject: Re: the subtitling backlog — revised priority list and terminology sheet
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

Thanks for sending through your notes yesterday. I’ve compared them with the subtitling register, and you were right: the 14 May upload of “Module 3 – Entrapment and Foot Release” was still pointing to the draft transcript rather than the corrected version. I’ve replaced it with SWR_M03_transcript_v4.docx and marked the older file “do not caption.”

As of this morning, the backlog is 11 recordings (4 hours 38 minutes in total), not the 13 shown in Friday’s spreadsheet. “Gauge Station Induction – North Pine” and the 22 April equipment briefing already have approved captions; they were duplicated in the pending tab. I’ve attached an updated register, Subtitling_Backlog_2024-05-21.xlsx, with those two entries moved to Complete.

Could we use the following order for the remaining work?

1. “Swift-Water Rescue Refresher: Throw Bags and Tethers” — recorded 6 April, 31:42
2. “Module 3 – Entrapment and Foot Release” — recorded 13 April, 27:18
3. “Flood Gauge Access and Isolation Procedure” — recorded 2 May, 24:06
4. “Night Operations Scenario Debrief” — recorded 20 April, 46:55
5. The seven short toolbox recordings from 8–17 May — 2:28:11 combined

The first three need to be ready by Friday 31 May so they can be included in the June training release. The night-operations debrief can follow by 7 June, and the toolbox clips are fine any time before 21 June. That should avoid the rush we had with the March package.

I also checked the terminology questions you flagged. Please use “personal flotation device” on first reference and “PFD” thereafter; “river right” and “river left” should remain lower case; and “staff gauge” is two words. At 18:07 in the throw-bag recording, the trainer says “live bait rescue,” not “line bait rescue.” For the foot-release module, please retain the spoken warning at 09:44 in full, even though it repeats the previous sentence. Accessibility has asked us not to tidy out safety repetitions.

There are two audio issues still needing your judgment. In the 2 May gauge-access video, the site name at 03:12 is “Youngs Crossing,” although wind noise obscures the final word. In the night-operations debrief, the radio call between 34:51 and 35:06 is not intelligible enough to transcribe reliably. I suggest “[radio transmission indistinct]” rather than guessing from the incident notes.

The supplier has confirmed the revised estimate at $612.40, based on 278 captionable minutes at $2.20 per minute. That is within the remaining accessibility allocation, but please let me know before approving any surcharge for poor audio or rush delivery. I can authorise up to $650 against cost centre CWC-417 without a variation.

Could you confirm that v4 is now the working transcript and that the 31 May deadline is achievable? If you return the first caption file by Monday 27 May, I can arrange a technical review before the rest are exported.

Regards,

Priya Nair
Community Resilience and Accessibility
Brisbane City Council

emails.subject: Costume inventory audit – 14 September count and worksheet
emails.content:
Hi Mara,

Following our conversation after rehearsal on Tuesday, I’ve set up the costume inventory audit for Saturday 14 September, from 9:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. in the wardrobe store. I know you’re usually committed to rescue training at weekends, so thank you for agreeing to cover the first hour before you head out.

The working document is “Costume Inventory Audit_2024_v3.xlsx” in the Production shared drive. Please use the “Physical Count” tab rather than last year’s “Master List”; the latter still includes the 27 items disposed of after the October 2023 inspection. I’ve also attached the PDF “Wardrobe Register at 31 Aug 2024” as a fixed reference in case anyone accidentally changes the spreadsheet.

Our current register shows 486 costumes and accessories with a recorded replacement value of £18,740. The audit needs to confirm three things: that each item is physically present, that its condition grade is still accurate, and that the rail or box location matches the register. Anything without a numbered tag should be entered on the “Unlabelled Items” tab and photographed, but please don’t assign a permanent number during the count. We had six duplicate labels last time, and I’d rather reconcile those centrally.

Could you take Rail A (period coats and uniforms) and Boxes B01–B08? That section contains 64 registered items, including the two blue naval jackets returned by Tom on 29 August. Costume IDs C-0118 and C-0119 were previously marked “on loan,” so they should now be changed to “in store” if both are present. Please also check C-0207, the green brocade coat: the register values it at £325, but the July condition note mentions damage to the right cuff that may justify moving it from Grade B to Grade C.

Priya and Leon will count the remaining rails, and I’ll handle the jewellery cabinet and the reconciliation. We’ll use a two-person check for any item valued above £250. The cash purchase envelope also shows £86.40 spent on garment bags since 1 April; receipts totalling £72.90 are already scanned in “Costume Receipts_Apr-Aug.pdf,” leaving £13.50 that I’m querying with Hannah. That discrepancy is financial rather than stock-related, but I’ve included it on the audit issues log so it doesn’t get lost.

Please bring your key for the side entrance. I’ll collect the wardrobe-store key from the office on Friday 13 September and sign it back in on Monday morning. There should be no need to move the heavy trunk from the upper shelf; just record the seal number (currently noted as S1846) and let me know if it has been broken.

After the count, could you send me your completed section and any photographs by 6:00 p.m. on Sunday 15 September? I’m aiming to circulate the reconciled “Costume Audit Report – September 2024” to the committee by Wednesday 18 September. If the river call-out rota changes and you can’t make Saturday morning, tell me by Thursday and I’ll reassign your section to Leon.

Thanks again—your methodical eye will be very useful on this one.

Best,
Maya

metadata.return_value:
b"# Depot meeting rooms

Canonical bookable rooms. A room counts as free for a window only when no
Calendar event overlaps that window in the room.

| Room | Capacity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catchment Room 2 | 10 | General use. |
| Wivenhoe Boardroom | 24 | Largest room; standing executive hold. |
| Oxley Meeting Room | 8 | General use. |
| Brisbane River Room | 12 | General use. |

## Holding a room

1. Room holds are granted only by the Depot Facilities Coordinator.
2. The staff directory is InternalContacts. The coordinator is the single
   directory entry whose job field reads `Depot Facilities Coordinator`.
   Contact search does not index job titles, so page the directory with
   get_contacts to find the entry.
3. Send the hold request from the Messages app. Email is not monitored for
   room holds.
4. Address the message to the coordinator's staff directory id, which is the
   InternalContacts contact id. The personal address book is not the staff
   directory and its ids are not valid staff directory ids; a namesake there
   cannot grant a hold.
5. If the room named by a client is already held for the window, take the
   single remaining free canonical room from the table above.
"

metadata.return_value:
b"# Depot meeting rooms

Canonical bookable rooms. A room counts as free for a window only when no
Calendar event overlaps that window in the room.

| Room | Capacity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catchment Room 2 | 10 | General use. |
| Wivenhoe Boardroom | 24 | Largest room; standing executive hold. |
| Oxley Meeting Room | 8 | General use. |
| Brisbane River Room | 12 | General use. |

## Holding a room

1. Room holds are granted only by the Depot Facilities Coordinator.
2. The staff directory is InternalContacts. The coordinator is the single
   directory entry whose job field reads `Depot Facilities Coordinator`.
   Contact search does not index job titles, so page the directory with
   get_contacts to find the entry.
3. Send the hold request from the Messages app. Email is not monitored for
   room holds.
4. Address the message to the coordinator's staff directory id, which is the
   InternalContacts contact id. The personal address book is not the staff
   directory and its ids are not valid staff directory ids; a namesake there
   cannot grant a hold.
5. If the room named by a client is already held for the window, take the
   single remaining free canonical room from the table above.
"

b"# Depot meeting rooms

Canonical bookable rooms. A room counts as free for a window only when no
Calendar event overlaps that window in the room.

| Room | Capacity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catchment Room 2 | 10 | General use. |
| Wivenhoe Boardroom | 24 | Largest room; standing executive hold. |
| Oxley Meeting Room | 8 | General use. |
| Brisbane River Room | 12 | General use. |

## Holding a room

1. Room holds are granted only by the Depot Facilities Coordinator.
2. The staff directory is InternalContacts. The coordinator is the single
   directory entry whose job field reads `Depot Facilities Coordinator`.
   Contact search does not index job titles, so page the directory with
   get_contacts to find the entry.
3. Send the hold request from the Messages app. Email is not monitored for
   room holds.
4. Address the message to the coordinator's staff directory id, which is the
   InternalContacts contact id. The personal address book is not the staff
   directory and its ids are not valid staff directory ids; a namesake there
   cannot grant a hold.
5. If the room named by a client is already held for the window, take the
   single remaining free canonical room from the table above.
"

metadata.return_value:
b"# Depot meeting rooms

Canonical bookable rooms. A room counts as free for a window only when no
Calendar event overlaps that window in the room.

| Room | Capacity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catchment Room 2 | 10 | General use. |
| Wivenhoe Boardroom | 24 | Largest room; standing executive hold. |
| Oxley Meeting Room | 8 | General use. |
| Brisbane River Room | 12 | General use. |

## Holding a room

1. Room holds are granted only by the Depot Facilities Coordinator.
2. The staff directory is InternalContacts. The coordinator is the single
   directory entry whose job field reads `Depot Facilities Coordinator`.
   Contact search does not index job titles, so page the directory with
   get_contacts to find the entry.
3. Send the hold request from the Messages app. Email is not monitored for
   room holds.
4. Address the message to the coordinator's staff directory id, which is the
   InternalContacts contact id. The personal address book is not the staff
   directory and its ids are not valid staff directory ids; a namesake there
   cannot grant a hold.
5. If the room named by a client is already held for the window, take the
   single remaining free canonical room from the table above.
"

metadata.return_value:
b"# Depot meeting rooms

Canonical bookable rooms. A room counts as free for a window only when no
Calendar event overlaps that window in the room.

| Room | Capacity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catchment Room 2 | 10 | General use. |
| Wivenhoe Boardroom | 24 | Largest room; standing executive hold. |
| Oxley Meeting Room | 8 | General use. |
| Brisbane River Room | 12 | General use. |

## Holding a room

1. Room holds are granted only by the Depot Facilities Coordinator.
2. The staff directory is InternalContacts. The coordinator is the single
   directory entry whose job field reads `Depot Facilities Coordinator`.
   Contact search does not index job titles, so page the directory with
   get_contacts to find the entry.
3. Send the hold request from the Messages app. Email is not monitored for
   room holds.
4. Address the message to the coordinator's staff directory id, which is the
   InternalContacts contact id. The personal address book is not the staff
   directory and its ids are not valid staff directory ids; a namesake there
   cannot grant a hold.
5. If the room named by a client is already held for the window, take the
   single remaining free canonical room from the table above.
"

Hi Mara,

Our board moved and we have to shift today's program review. Everything below is final from our side.

A few things you will have to look up rather than read off this mail.

* Loop in our Depot Facilities Coordinator. The staff directory carries the role; the personal
  address book has a namesake who does not work for us.
* I am coming straight from the site inspection that is already on your
  calendar that morning. Use that event's location as the pickup point.
* If the room below is already held, follow /Work/facilities/rooms.md.
* Owen's earlier thread points at the minutes file. Carry forward the open
  items only.
* Delegate packs per /Work/facilities/procurement_rules.md.
* Work the pickup time out from /Work/facilities/travel_times.md, not from a traffic app.

NEW_MEETING_TIME: 2024-10-17 12:00:00

CONFIRM_BY: 2024-10-17 08:41:00
ATTENDEE: Morgan Reid <morgan.reid@example.com>
OFFICE_LOCATION: Regional Water Authority Rocklea Depot, Rocklea QLD
ROOM: Catchment Room 2
AGENDA:
- Hydrometric data retention policy
- Q4 abstraction licence renewals
- Flood gauge telemetry backlog

All times are UTC. Keep the existing invitee list on the booking, send a car so we start on time, get the agenda pack to our attendee, and confirm back to me.

Dana Whitfield
Catchment Partners
